---
title: "Flight-level crossings"
description: "How OPDI finds every crossing of flight levels 50, 70, 100 and 245 (xing-fl50, xing-fl70, xing-fl100, xing-fl245)."
---

## In one sentence

An `xing-fl{level}` event marks each moment the aircraft climbs or descends
through flight level 50, 70, 100 or 245.

## What it needs

- The cleaned barometric altitude of the track's reports, with the same
  plausibility limits as the [tops](tops.qmd). A **flight level** is the
  altitude in hundreds of feet on the standard pressure of 1013.25 hPa:
  flight level 100 (FL100) is 10,000 ft on the altimeter.
- Positions near the crossing, for its position.

## How it is computed

1. For each level, follow the altitude of the track in time order.
2. **Dead band.** To ignore small movements around a level, a band of 300 ft
   on each side is used: the aircraft counts as above FL100 only once it is
   above 10,300 ft, and as below only once it is below 9,700 ft; inside the
   band it keeps the side it was last on. A crossing is the moment the side
   changes. A flight that levels off at the level itself never leaves the
   band and has no crossing of it.
3. **Time.** The time is interpolated in a straight line between the two
   reports either side of the level itself; the event's altitude is exactly
   the level. Reports without an altitude are skipped. When the two reports
   are more than 30 minutes apart, no crossing is given, because its time
   cannot be placed.
4. **Position.** One of the two reports often has no position. It then takes
   the position interpolated between the nearest reports with a position
   before and after it, each at most 30 s away; otherwise the position stays
   empty.
5. **Position jumps.** A position that jumps away from the track and back
   (one or two reports whose steps to their neighbours imply more than
   1,000 kt, with 2 NM of tolerance) is treated as missing. A crossing whose
   two reports still imply more than 1,000 kt is not given.
6. Every crossing is kept and numbered in time order (`info.crossing_seq`).

## Based on

- Developed for OPDI. The same crossing method (a dead band, then
  interpolation) serves the [distance circles](distance-rings.qmd) and the
  [runway threshold crossing](xing-runway-threshold.qmd).

## What is published

Event types `xing-fl50`, `xing-fl70`, `xing-fl100` and `xing-fl245` (the
family `xing-fl{level}`), with position, altitude, `distance_flown_nm` and
`time_passed_s`. Their `info` holds `crossing_seq`, `direction` (`up` or
`down`) and `bracket_s`, the time between the two reports the crossing was
placed between (see the [Data dictionary](../data/dictionary.qmd#info-fields)).

## Use cases

- **Climb and descent times**: from `ATOT` to the first `xing-fl100` up, or
  from the last `xing-fl100` down to `ALDT`.
- **Interrupted climbs**: several crossings of the same level on one flight
  show a climb or descent that went back through it.
- **Traffic in the upper airspace**: counts of `xing-fl245` crossings per
  region.

## Limitations

A crossing between reports far apart in time is an estimate (see
`info.bracket_s`). See
[Limitations: vertical profile](../limitations.qmd#lim-vertical).
